title: Streamlined prefetch bridge for variable page-size dashboard API
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Console dashboard queries exhibit high tail latency and read amplification when clients request variable page sizes (1..200 rows) across tenant-scoped time series. Current implementations either over-fetch (wasted I/O) or under-fetch (many small reads), and the cursor system does not provide a compact index that supports both fast random-access pages and efficient sequential scans. Goal: Ship a 'prefetch bridge' that dynamically chooses between sequential prefetch, bounded read-ahead, and indexed point-reads per request, using a compact per-tenant hot-window summary to predict likely next pages. Success metrics: reduce 95th percentile page latency for page_size<=200 to <250ms on p95 at 1k QPS; lower total read amplification by >=35%; reduce average DB request count per UI page by >=40%. Approach summary: 1) Add a small in-memory tenant hot-window sketch (reservoir + exponential decay counters) updated by recent console query traces to identify hot shards and likely next offsets. 2) Implement a 'prefetch bridge' at the dashboard query API layer that: a) for sequential patterns uses adaptive read-ahead with exponential backing-off when no further pages are requested; b) for random-access patterns issues a compact index lookup (time + shard -> byte range) to issue a single point read; c) fallbacks to existing segmented cursor flow if predictions are low-confidence. 3) Introduce a read-path circuit breaker to keep latency SLOs: if bridge latency risk exceeds threshold, route to fastest compatible variant. 4) Materialize optional lightweight page manifests for heavy-report tenants (configurable). Design trade-offs: extra memory per-tenant for the hot-window summary vs latency savings; potential slight increase in write-path metadata during cursor creation; predictability vs complexity of heuristic tuning. Migration/rollout: feature flag by tenant + rollout group, start with internal alpha tenants, expand to heavy-read SaaS customers, then default-on with conservative thresholds. Observability: add per-request route tags, bridge_decision enum, prefetch_bytes and db_read_count metrics, tracing spans for prediction and read stages, and a dashboard with cost delta and SLOs. Backwards compatibility: cursors remain interoperable; bridging is an opt-in layer that does not change cursor encoding. Implementation plan: - Prototype prefetch sketch and bridge logic in a standalone service behind feature flag. - Add small Cassandra/Postgres schema for optional manifests. - Client-visible API unchanged; server-side decisioning only. - Integration tests for sequential, random, and mixed workloads. - Load test harness against staging with synthetic tenant mix to verify cost/latency.
